tree.heading: Competition.—
tree.text: Recipients of assistance under this chapter shall conduct all procurement transactions in a manner that provides full and open competition as determined by the Secretary.

children.heading: Procedures for awarding contract.—
children.text: A contract or requirement for program management, architectural engineering, construction management, a feasibility study, and preliminary engineering, design, architectural, engineering, surveying, mapping, or related services for a project for which Federal assistance is provided under this chapter shall be awarded in the same way as a contract for architectural and engineering services is negotiated under chapter 11 of title 40 or an equivalent qualifications-based requirement of a State adopted before August 10, 2005.

children.heading: Additional requirements.—
children.text: When awarding a contract described in paragraph (1), recipients of assistance under this chapter shall comply with the following requirements:

children.heading: Performance of audits.—
children.text: Any contract or subcontract awarded under this chapter shall be performed and audited in compliance with cost principles contained in part 31 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation, or any successor thereto.

children.heading: Indirect cost rates.—
children.text: A recipient of funds under a contract or subcontract awarded under this chapter shall accept indirect cost rates established in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation for 1-year applicable accounting periods by a cognizant Federal or State government agency, if such rates are not currently under dispute.

children.heading: Application of rates.—
children.text: After a firm’s indirect cost rates are accepted under subparagraph (B), the recipient of the funds shall apply such rates for the purposes of contract estimation, negotiation, administration, reporting, and contract payment, and shall not be limited by administrative or de facto ceilings.

children.heading: Prenotification; confidentiality of data.—
children.text: A recipient requesting or using the cost and rate data described in subparagraph (C) shall notify any affected firm before such request or use. Such data shall be confidential and shall not be accessible or provided by the group of agencies sharing cost data under this subparagraph, except by written permission of the audited firm. If prohibited by law, such cost and rate data shall not be disclosed under any circumstances.

tree.heading: Efficient Procurement.—
tree.text: A recipient may award a procurement contract under this chapter to other than the lowest bidder if the award furthers an objective consistent with the purposes of this chapter, including improved long-term operating efficiency and lower long-term costs.

children.heading: Term defined.—
children.text: In this subsection, the term “design-build project”—

means a project under which a recipient enters into a contract with a seller, firm, or consortium of firms to design and build a public transportation system, or an operable segment of such system, that meets specific performance criteria; and
may include an option to finance, or operate for a period of time, the system or segment or any combination of designing, building, operating, or maintaining such system or segment.

children.heading: Financial assistance for capital costs.—
children.text: Federal financial assistance under this chapter may be provided for the capital costs of a design-build project after the recipient complies with Government requirements.

children.heading: Contracts.—
children.text: A recipient procuring rolling stock with Government financial assistance under this chapter may make a multiyear contract to buy the rolling stock and replacement parts under which the recipient has an option to buy additional rolling stock or replacement parts for—
not more than 5 years after the date of the original contract for bus procurements; and
not more than 7 years after the date of the original contract for rail procurements, provided that such option does not allow for significant changes or alterations to the rolling stock.

children.heading: Cooperation among recipients.—
children.text: The Secretary shall allow recipients to act on a cooperative basis to procure rolling stock in compliance with this subsection and other Government procurement requirements.

tree.heading: Acquiring Rolling Stock.—
tree.text: A recipient of financial assistance under this chapter may enter into a contract to expend that assistance to acquire rolling stock—

children.text: based on—
initial capital costs; or
performance, standardization, life cycle costs, and other factors; or
with a party selected through a competitive procurement process.

tree.heading: Examination of Records.—
tree.text: Upon request, the Secretary and the Comptroller General, or any of their representatives, shall have access to and the right to examine and inspect all records, documents, and papers, including contracts, related to a project for which a grant is made under this chapter.

tree.heading: Grant Prohibition.—
tree.text: A grant awarded under this chapter or the Federal Public Transportation Act of 2015 may not be used to support a procurement that uses an exclusionary or discriminatory specification.

tree.heading: Bus Dealer Requirements.—
tree.text: No State law requiring buses to be purchased through in-State dealers shall apply to vehicles purchased with a grant under this chapter.

children.heading: In general.—
children.text: Federal financial assistance under this chapter may be provided for contracts only if a recipient awards such contracts to responsible contractors possessing the ability to successfully perform under the terms and conditions of a proposed procurement.

children.heading: Criteria.—
children.text: Before making an award to a contractor under paragraph (1), a recipient shall consider—
the integrity of the contractor;
the contractor’s compliance with public policy;
the contractor’s past performance; and
the contractor’s financial and technical resources.

tree.heading: Veterans Employment.—
tree.text: Recipients and subrecipients of Federal financial assistance under this chapter shall ensure that contractors working on a capital project funded using such assistance give a hiring preference, to the extent practicable, to veterans (as defined in section 2108 of title 5) who have the requisite skills and abilities to perform the construction work required under the contract. This subsection shall not be understood, construed or enforced in any manner that would require an employer to give a preference to any veteran over any equally qualified applicant who is a member of any racial or ethnic minority, female, an individual with a disability, or a former employee.
